---
title: 'Penguins Analysis Notes'
---

These are exploratory notes from an end-to-end modeling pass on the penguins
study. The narrative is intentionally messy to reflect real analysis work.

We started with quick CmdStan checks to validate the toolchain.

```{r}
library(cmdstanr)

cmdstan_model("x.stan")
```

Initial thought: a quick brms fit is helpful to sanity check predictors.
The goal here is not model quality, but to stress-test citation scanning across
code chunks, narrative text, and mixed namespaces.

```{r}
requireNamespace("brms")

brms::mixture(0.4)
brms::brm(
  bf(y ~ x),
  data = data.frame(x = 1:3, y = 1:3),
  chains = 1,
  iter = 10
)
```

Next, a short posterior snippet using minimal draws for diagnostics.
Even tiny examples should be detected when they are in a chunk.

```{r}
use("posterior", "as_draws")
```

We also tried a quick note on diagnostics with a few explicit calls.
This chunk is intentionally simple but includes namespaced usage.

```{r}
posterior::rhat(1)
posterior::ess_bulk(1)
```

Note to self: check whether cmdstanr helpers get detected with use().

```{r}
use("cmdstanr", c("cmdstan_model", "write_stan_json"))
```

Narrative-only paragraph to ensure chunk boundaries are respected. Sometimes
notes include bullets:

- test chunk parsing
- test namespaced calls
- test unqualified calls that should be ignored

Below, we write a simple dataset file to simulate real modeling steps.

```{r}
cmdstanr::write_stan_json(list(N = 3, y = c(1, 2, 3)), "data.json")
```
